Let’s be completely clear about what we are witnessing here: this is the direct result of a fundamentally rigged economic order that prioritizes the hoarded wealth of property owners and landlords over the basic human right to housing. While the ruling establishment gaslights the public by spinning statistics, working-class and vulnerable communities are paying the devastating human price for policies designed to protect the status quo. 

We saw this exact systemic cruelty in Limerick just this past week, when Taoiseach Micheál Martin had the absolute nerve to boast that housing tenancies have increased, completely glossing over the human cost of his own administration's policies. Sure, the Government pats itself on the back for introducing new rules on March 1 forcing landlords to provide six-year leases for tenants, but it's completely half-hearted. It leaves gaping loopholes that landlords can weaponize against tenants to protect their profit margins. 

The reality on the ground—which the establishment actively tries to sweep under the rug—is a shameful rise in eviction notices and homelessness, with the numbers of people in emergency accommodation nationally increasing again. Instead of confronting the deep structural inequality driving this housing crisis, they are just pushing the most vulnerable people right out onto the streets.
